evidence.note: Strong opening orientation: read workspace/crate Cargo.toml and stubs, mined common/api-server/scheduler/controller-manager tests, listed the reference tree, and read core/v1 types.go, TypeMeta and ObjectMeta from /opt/k8s-reference to derive camelCase/optional-field contracts and dependency order.

The only steps where /opt/k8s-reference is actually read via commands. After step 15 the reference is never re-consulted; 'Read reference Go types' recurs only as unexecuted plan text (e.g. lines 123-202), showing the source-of-truth grounding was not sustained.

Test mining continued but narrowed to ~8 files (pod_handler, configmap, ipaddress, servicecidr, scheduler); contracts were inferred from tests, not the reference. Level-5-style per-crate reading held for early crates only.
Shifted to bulk Python codegen and killing builds to iterate faster; later crates (kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, cloud-providers) were generated without reading their test contracts.

Back half is compile-error-driven: fixing import paths, duplicate types, and guessing struct shapes rather than re-consulting reference or tests. No mention anywhere of the hidden conformance suite or conformance-vs-fixture distinction (grep for 'conformance/hidden/black-box' returns nothing).

reasoning: The agent opened with solid level-5 behavior for the leaf crates — reading tests and Cargo.toml, consulting the upstream reference for ObjectMeta/TypeMeta, and grasping the dependency order. But this was not sustained: the reference was actually read only through step 15 and thereafter appeared only as unexecuted plan boilerplate, later crates were codegen'd/guessed without reading their tests, and there was zero awareness of the hidden conformance suite. That places it above anchor 3 (genuine reference use, multi-crate test reading, dependency-order understanding) but below a clean anchor 5 (no whole-surface mapping, reference abandoned, fixture/error-driven for the back half), i.e. a 4.
